title: Brutal
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Hiroki Dan is a polite, well-liked homicide detective and the son of a former police chief. In secret he is a serial killer who tortures and kills people he believes the law cannot reach, such as abusers, rapists and a man profiting from his past murders. Each chapter is largely a self-contained case.
life_message: It presents private, violent retribution against unpunished abusers as a dark fantasy of justice, without resolving whether it is justice.

content.note: Prolonged torture and dismemberment fitted to each victim's crime (Bleeding Cool; AniList Torture, Gore, Sadism).
Described by a critic as one of the darkest manga of its decade; horror and thriller genres (Bleeding Cool; AniList).
Rape is part of victims' backstories, including a cult that assaults women; nudity (AniList Rape, Nudity tags; Bleeding Cool). Depiction detail to verify.
Harsh and abusive speech from targets likely (to verify).
Possible drugging and drinking in some cases (to verify).
Abuse and bullying themes; a tabloid reporter hounds people to suicide (MangaUpdates categories Abuse, Bullying via batch data; Bleeding Cool).
A police officer as vigilante torturer, framed sympathetically against abusers (Bleeding Cool; AniList Anti-Hero, Sadism).

dominant: Vigilante retribution; rage at misogyny and abuse; failure of the law

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Dan answers wrongs personally and violently rather than through the courts he serves.

Order vs freedom.evidence: He acts entirely outside police rules and institutional oversight.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Targets are strangers who harmed others; motive is general, not family.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Elite and powerful offenders are targeted; Dan himself is from police elite.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Calculated, secular procedural world; no religious frame for justice.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Fear, threat and punishment dominate every case.

folkways.japan: Critics read it against Japanese debates on low conviction of sexual abusers and on public politeness masking private harm (tatemae and honne).

delivery.evidence: Vigilante crime episodes per AniList summary (credited to ANN); no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: The justice question is posed through episodes of retribution rather than resolved in narration.

winners_losers: Dan wins case after case and is never caught in the arcs described; abusers lose horrifically. Sympathy goes to victims and, uneasily, to the vigilante.
